title: Detoxifying Language Models Risks Marginalizing Minority Voices
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures how detoxification techniques degrade Language Model (LM) performance, specifically perplexity and human-rated generation quality, on non-toxic text that contains minority identity mentions, including religious identities like 'Muslim' and 'Jew'.
findings: Detoxification techniques, which aim to reduce toxic output, were found to disproportionately harm the model's utility on language containing minority identity mentions, including religious terms like 'Muslim'. This leads to higher perplexity and lower-quality text generation for such inputs. The paper highlights a practical harm where a detoxified chatbot could discuss Christianity but was unable to discuss Islam, demonstrating that these methods can silence conversations about minority religions.
